How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Questions to ask the vendor (3)

  1. How many people work for GitHub, and how many of them work in engineering, security and customer support?
    Headcount indicates capacity to support a large bank deployment.
  2. Has GitHub carried out any workforce reductions in the last 24 months, and which functions were affected?
    Workforce reductions can signal reduced support capacity.
  3. Has any regulated financial-services customer stopped using GitHub Copilot or GitHub Advanced Security in the last 24 months, and why?
    Loss of major customers can indicate product or service problems.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-17 · launch GitHub
    GitHub Copilot app adds GA support for GitHub Enterprise Server; browser use enters preview

    GitHub's changelog of 17 November 2026 says the GitHub Copilot app's support for GitHub Enterprise Server accounts is now generally available, and that Azure DevOps repository support and browser use, in which Copilot operates a Chromium-based browser in an isolated tab group, are in public preview. The entry says browser use is off by default and states no plan or pricing changes. GitHub (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-11-17 · launch GitHub
    GitHub puts on-demand secret scanning in Copilot's security review into public preview

    GitHub's changelog of 17 November 2026 says Copilot's security review now runs GitHub's secret scanning detectors on code changes before merge, in public preview, across Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, Copilot SDK integrations and Copilot code review. The entry says the feature is off by default, is not yet in VS Code, and that scans consume AI credits under the Secret Protection AI Credit SKU. GitHub (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-11-16 · outage GitHub
    GitHub reports roughly six-hour degradation of pull requests, Actions and Git operations

    According to GitHub's status page, an incident on 16 November 2026 degraded pull requests, GitHub Actions and Git push and fetch latency, with impact from about 09:30 to 15:55 UTC. GitHub's post-incident summary attributes it to storage servers holding Git repository data reaching disk read bandwidth limits during a planned repository migration, made worse by a disk configuration setting, and says the same cause produced a shorter event on 13 November. GitHub (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  4. 2026-09-16 · litigation GitHubOpenAIMicrosoft
    Ninth Circuit affirms dismissal of DMCA claim against GitHub, Microsoft and OpenAI over Copilot

    Reported by The Next Web on 2026-09-18 and PPC Land on 2026-09-20: in Doe v. GitHub (No. 24-7700) a Ninth Circuit panel on 2026-09-16 affirmed dismissal of the programmers' Digital Millennium Copyright Act claim that GitHub Copilot and OpenAI's Codex model removed copyright management information, holding that the tools generate new output. Both outlets reported that two breach-of-contract claims remain pending in the Northern District of California. The Next Web (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)PPC Land (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  5. 2026-06-01 · pricing change GitHub
    GitHub Copilot moves from premium requests to token-metered AI Credits

    GitHub announced on 2026-04-27 that from 2026-06-01 Copilot premium request units would be replaced by GitHub AI Credits consumed by token usage at each model's published rate, with pooled credits and budget controls for organisations. Seat prices were unchanged at US$19 for Copilot Business and US$39 for Copilot Enterprise; code completions stay unmetered. GitHub (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  6. 2026-05-18 · security incident GitHub
    GitHub discloses theft of about 3,800 internal repositories via poisoned VS Code extension

    GitHub disclosed on 2026-05-20 that it had detected on 2026-05-18 the compromise of an employee device through a poisoned third-party VS Code extension, and that an attacker's claim to have taken about 3,800 GitHub-internal repositories was directionally consistent with its investigation. GitHub stated it had no evidence of impact on customer information outside those repositories, some of which hold customer information such as support excerpts, and that it rotated secrets including the Enterprise Server signing key. Reported also by SecurityWeek on 2026-05-20 and BleepingComputer on 2026-05-21. GitHub's update of 2026-05-26 said the investigation was continuing. GitHub (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)SecurityWeek (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)BleepingComputer (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

    GitHub chief executive Thomas Dohmke announces departure; GitHub continues within Microsoft CoreAI
